steps.body: The last dial sits INSIDE: y = sin(bx). The b is a horizontal squeeze — at b = 2 the input races twice as fast, finishing a full lap in half the room. The rule: **period = 2π/b**. Bigger b, faster wave, SHORTER period.

dials.feedback: The wave is not repeating at the right rate. The b in sin(bx) counts how many full cycles fit where one used to.

widget.prompt: Set the dial to build y = sin(2x), then read how far it travels before repeating.
widget.successFeedback: Period π ≈ 3.14 — half of 2π, because b = 2 packs two cycles into the space of one. Period = 2π ÷ b, and the dial makes the division visible rather than remembered.
widget.lowFeedback: The wave is still stretched — fewer cycles than y = sin(2x).
widget.highFeedback: The wave is compressed past y = sin(2x) — too many cycles.

explanationVariants: b = 1/2 stretches the wave out: period = 2π/(1/2) = 4π ≈ 12.57.
Dividing by a half doubles — a slow wave needs twice the room.

widget.prompt: What is the period of y = cos(x/2)?

options.label: 4π
options.feedback: Yes — period = 2π/|b|, and dividing 2π by 1/2 doubles it to 4π. A b below 1 stretches the wave.

options.label: π
options.feedback: π is 2π × (1/2) — multiplied BY b instead of divided. Dividing by a half doubles: 2π/(1/2) = 4π.

options.label: 2π
options.feedback: 2π leaves the wave unstretched — but b = 1/2 slows it, DOUBLING the period to 4π.

options.label: π/4
options.feedback: π/4 shrinks the period, which is what a b ABOVE 1 does. Here b = 1/2 is below 1, so the wave stretches.

steps.body: Designing a wave runs the rule backward: **b = 2π/period**. Want a wave that repeats every π/2? Then b = 2π ÷ (π/2) = 4. The check never lies: b × period must equal 2π, always.

widget.prompt: You want y = sin(bx) to have period π/2. What is b?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.25 is period/2π — the fraction flipped. b = 2π/period = 4 (and 4 · π/2 = 2π checks).
b = 2 gives period π — twice the target. Repeating every π/2 needs b = 4.

explanationVariants: The period's denominator becomes b when the period is 2π-over-something.

widget.prompt: y = sin(bx) has period 2π/3. What is b?

commonErrors.feedback: 0.33 is 1/3 — inverted. b = 2π divided by the period: 3.
6 doubles it — check: b · period = 6 · 2π/3 = 4π ≠ 2π. The product test demands b = 3.

steps.body: All three dials assemble into **y = a sin(bx) + d**: amplitude → a, midline → d, period → b = 2π/period. Given any wave description, fill the three slots in that order — each read is independent of the others.

widget.prompt: A wave has midline 5, amplitude 2, and period π. Which rule fits?

options.label: y = 5 sin(2x) + 2
options.feedback: a and d swapped — the 5 is the CENTER (added at the end), the 2 is the swing (multiplying the sine).

options.label: y = 2 sin(x) + 5
options.feedback: b = 1 leaves the period at 2π — a π-period wave needs b = 2π/π = 2.

options.label: y = 2 sin(πx) + 5
options.feedback: b = π gives period 2π/π = 2, not π — b is 2π DIVIDED BY the period, not the period itself.

explanationVariants: The b multiplies the INPUT before sine ever sees it — inside first.

widget.prompt: For y = 3 sin(2x) + 1, find the value at x = π/4.

commonErrors.feedback: 3.12 is 3 sin(π/4) + 1 — the b never fired. Inside first: 2 · π/4 = π/2, and sin(π/2) = 1, so y = 4.
3 drops the +1 — the midline shift applies last: 3 · 1 + 1 = 4.

hints: Work inside-out: multiply the input by b first.
2 · π/4 = π/2 — and sin(π/2) is the wave's peak value.

takeaways: Period = 2π/b — bigger b, faster wave, shorter repeat.
y = a sin(bx) + d assembles amplitude, speed, and midline independently.
steps.teaser: Next: aiming all three dials at the real world — ferris wheels, tides, and the identity that ties sine to cosine.

concept.body: One period computation, cleanly. y = sin(4x): the 4 makes the input run four times as fast, so the wave finishes in a quarter of the room — period = 2π/4 = π/2 ≈ 1.57. Divide 2π by b; that's the whole rule.

explanationVariants: Four times the speed, one-quarter the period.

widget.prompt: What is the period of y = sin(4x)? (Round to hundredths.)

commonErrors.feedback: 25.13 is 4 · 2π — multiplied. Faster waves have SHORTER periods: 2π/4 ≈ 1.57.
6.28 ignores the 4 — the squeeze cuts the period to a quarter: ≈ 1.57.
